quarterly_data.signal: CEO Sanjay Mehrotra: fiscal 2026 revenue was 3 1/2 times last year's record, with data center revenue up fourfold, and Micron's DRAM revenue for fiscal year 2026 surpassed $100 billion. CFO Mark Murphy: record fiscal 2026 revenue of $133.2 billion, up 256% year over year; fiscal 2026 gross margins expanded to 81.1%, a 40-percentage point improvement from fiscal 2025, and EPS increased 811% year over year to $75.52. Mehrotra: 'As strong as fiscal 2026 was, we expect fiscal 2027 to be even better. Industry demand has strengthened since our last earnings call.'
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 DRAM revenue surpassed $100 billion; FY2026 revenue $133.2 billion, up 256%; data center revenue up fourfold

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Mark Murphy: fiscal Q4 consolidated revenue was $54.2 billion, up 31% sequentially and up 379% year over year, the sixth consecutive quarterly revenue record. Fiscal Q4 DRAM revenue was a record $39.8 billion, up 343% year over year and 73% of total revenue, up 27% sequentially; DRAM bit shipments were up mid-single-digit percentage range and prices increased high-teens percentage range, driven by tight DRAM industry conditions. Consolidated gross margin was 87.0%, up 210 basis points sequentially, driven primarily by higher pricing and strong execution, partially offset by mix.
quarterly_data.figure: FQ4 DRAM revenue $39.8 billion (up 343% YoY, up 27% QoQ, 73% of revenue); DRAM prices up high-teens %, bits up mid-single-digit %; gross margin 87.0%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Mark Murphy, fiscal Q4 by business unit: Cloud Memory (CMBU) revenue a record $16.3 billion (30% of total), up 18% sequentially on higher pricing and bit shipments, with CMBU gross margins 83%, flat sequentially, as higher pricing was offset by higher HBM mix; Core Data Center (CDBU) a record $18.0 billion (33%), up 56% sequentially, gross margins 90%, up 290 basis points; Mobile and Client (MCBU) a record $13.1 billion (24%), up 14% sequentially on higher pricing, partially offset by lower bit shipments, gross margins 90%, up 260 basis points; Automotive and Embedded (AEBU) a record $6.8 billion (13%), up 47% sequentially on higher pricing and higher bit shipments, gross margins 84%, up 470 basis points.
quarterly_data.figure: MCBU $13.1 billion (gross margin 90%); AEBU $6.8 billion (gross margin 84%); CMBU gross margin 83%, flat on higher HBM mix; CDBU $18.0 billion (gross margin 90%)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Mark Murphy: with 26 strategic customer agreements (SCAs) signed in total, remaining performance obligations (RPO) are approximately $150 billion. RPO covers only SCAs with a determined pricing framework (fixed price or a pricing floor and ceiling), is based on committed volumes and minimum pricing and is 'inherently conservative'; Micron expects revenue to well exceed the associated RPO over the agreement terms. CEO Sanjay Mehrotra: the 26 SCAs are currently estimated at over 35% of Micron's revenue through 2030; Micron has now signed SCAs that extend into 2031, plus one-year extensions to 2031 for two agreements, and any new SCA discussions involving pricing are negotiated with higher pricing; financial commitments from customers for the signed SCAs and extensions increased to $32 billion, the vast majority cash deposits. Murphy: customer cash deposits received in fiscal Q4 were $12.3 billion, and customer cash deposits on the balance sheet at the end of fiscal Q4 were $12.7 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: RPO approximately $150 billion; 26 SCAs, over 35% of revenue through 2030; customer financial commitments $32 billion; SCAs extend into 2031

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Sanjay Mehrotra: Micron's HBM revenue in fiscal Q4 2026 grew faster than total company revenue, as Micron ramps HBM shipments across a growing number of customers (none named). Micron has completed agreements for the vast majority of its calendar 2027 HBM bit supply with significant price increases year over year, narrowing the gross margin gap with conventional DRAM, and continues to execute well on its HBM4 ramp. Micron expects industry HBM bit shipments to grow faster than conventional DRAM through calendar 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: vast majority of calendar 2027 HBM bit supply under completed agreements; FQ4 HBM revenue grew faster than total company revenue

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Sanjay Mehrotra, market outlook: memory and storage supply-demand conditions are expected to be much tighter in calendar 2027 and 2028 than they were in 2026. DRAM: calendar 2026 industry bit shipments expected to grow in the mid-20s percentage range, with Micron DRAM supply growing approximately in line with industry; calendar 2027 and 2028 industry DRAM bit shipments expected to grow approximately in the low-20s percentage range, with the industry remaining supply constrained in both years. Cleanroom additions are required to augment node-transition supply growth; even with additional industry DRAM cleanroom plans and with new upside requests from customers, 'we do not have line of sight to when supply and demand will return to balance.' Data center: server unit growth expected in the high-teens percentage range in both calendar 2026 and 2027, supported by a modestly lower rate of content growth than prior expectations, amid tight memory supply.
quarterly_data.figure: industry DRAM bits: mid-20s % in calendar 2026, low-20s % in calendar 2027 and 2028 (supply constrained); server units high-teens % in calendar 2026 and 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Manufacturing and capex, per CEO Sanjay Mehrotra and CFO Mark Murphy: Micron celebrated a concrete pour milestone for its first New York fab, with initial wafer output expected in calendar 2030; Idaho ID1 is on track to commence wafer output in mid-calendar 2027 and ID2 in late calendar 2028; in fiscal Q4 Micron held a groundbreaking for its DRAM fab expansion in Japan, with initial output expected in late calendar 2028 to support technology node transitions; the Taiwan Tongluo facility is on track for meaningful product shipments in mid-calendar 2027; at the Singapore HBM advanced packaging facility cleanroom preparation is ahead of plan, with initial output expected in early calendar 2027. 1-gamma DRAM and G9 NAND are Micron's largest production nodes today; next-generation DRAM and NAND nodes are on track to begin volume production in the second half of calendar 2027. Micron plans to increase fiscal 2027 capex versus prior plans; a majority of the increase is for construction capex, most of which is to help accelerate cleanroom space availability in late calendar 2028 and beyond, and optimizing production from available cleanroom space is resulting in some pull-forward of equipment spending; Murphy projects fiscal Q1 capex of around $11.5 billion, first-half fiscal 2027 capex of approximately $25 billion, higher capex in the second half of fiscal 2027, and a meaningfully higher growth rate in construction capex than equipment capex.
quarterly_data.figure: FQ1 FY2027 capex around $11.5 billion; 1H FY2027 capex approximately $25 billion; first New York fab output calendar 2030; Japan DRAM expansion output late calendar 2028; Singapore HBM packaging output early calendar 2027

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Sanjay Mehrotra: PC and mobile industry revenue remain on track to grow this calendar year, driven by the premium end, despite potential double-digit overall unit declines in both markets; nearly half of Mobile and Client Business Unit revenue in fiscal Q4 was generated by 1-gamma products. Physical AI: memory content in Level 4 and higher autonomous vehicles typically exceeds 200GB, while storage content reaches multiple terabytes, each more than an order of magnitude greater than in Level 2+ and Level 3 vehicles; humanoid robots are expected to have comparable requirements. Mehrotra: physical AI 'can become a significant driver of memory and storage demand by the end of this decade'; several physical AI customers (none named) are sampling Micron's next-generation products.
quarterly_data.figure: nearly half of FQ4 MCBU revenue from 1-gamma products; Level 4+ autonomous vehicle memory content typically exceeds 200GB

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Mark Murphy: Micron expects fiscal 2027 to be another record year, with sequential revenue growth each quarter. Fiscal Q1 is anticipated to be the floor for gross margins in fiscal 2027 (higher-cost inventories from the increased fiscal 2026 incentive compensation principally impact fiscal Q1), with higher gross margins beyond fiscal Q1 for the remainder of fiscal 2027 and a more moderate rate of price increases. Operating expenses are projected to increase by approximately $2.5 billion in fiscal 2027, primarily from higher R&D and higher incentive compensation. Fiscal Q4 ending inventory was $10.4 billion with days of inventory (DIO) at 129, up nine days sequentially (including node end-of-life-related build-ahead); 'Our inventory levels and supply remain extremely tight', and Murphy expects DIO to decline in the coming quarters.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2027: sequential revenue growth each quarter, FQ1 the gross-margin floor, opex up approximately $2.5 billion; FQ4 DIO 129

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Mark Murphy: fiscal Q4 NAND revenue was a record $14.1 billion, up 526% year over year and 26% of total revenue, up 42% sequentially; bit shipments increased approximately 10% and prices increased approximately 30%, driven by tight NAND industry conditions. CEO Sanjay Mehrotra: data center SSD revenue in fiscal Q4 was nearly $10 billion, more than 10 times the year-ago quarter and over two-thirds of total company NAND revenue; Micron is on track to deliver the fifth consecutive year of record market share in data center SSD in calendar 2026, with design wins across the largest data center deployments; AI context memory storage used for KV cache offload and HDD displacement are expanding the addressable market for SSDs.
quarterly_data.figure: FQ4 NAND revenue $14.1 billion (up 526% YoY, up 42% QoQ); data center SSD revenue nearly $10 billion, over two-thirds of NAND revenue

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Sanjay Mehrotra, NAND outlook: calendar 2026 industry NAND bit shipments are expected to grow in the low-20s percentage range, slightly above prior expectations, with Micron NAND supply growing less than industry supply growth in calendar 2026; for calendar 2027 and 2028 industry NAND bit shipments are expected to grow approximately in the mid-20s percentage range, with the industry remaining supply constrained in both years.
quarterly_data.figure: industry NAND bits: low-20s % in calendar 2026 (slightly above prior view); mid-20s % in calendar 2027 and 2028, supply constrained
